text:
alex: incident-bot just paged with a spike of 5xx + p95 latency on model variant `llama-prod-v3-canary`. seeing errors ~30% on requests. paging @maria (on-call).
incident-bot: INCIDENT CREATED: INC-2026-045 — High error rate and latency on model llama-prod-v3-canary. Severity: P1. Channel: #incidents. Pager: @maria.
maria: ack, I'm on it. pulling traces + logs now. any customer-facing alerts? @kevin any active rollouts that touch this variant?
kevin: I pushed a weight change for routing earlier today (small traffic to canary). didn't touch model artifacts. v3-canary was supposed to be 10% traffic. rolling that back now if that's helpful.
sophie: I'm watching metrics — p50 ok, p95 jumped from 120ms -> 1800ms and 5xx rate jumped to ~22% for the canary model only. Stable variant is fine.
alex: good signal. plan: reduce traffic to 0 for that variant (quick flip) and route traffic to `llama-prod-v3-stable`. also enable emergency rate limits for heavy keys until we confirm rollback.
maria: agreed. executing disable now.
kevin: here's the CLI I'm running:
```
# mark variant disabled and re-route
redwoodctl variants update --model llama-prod-v3 --variant canary --enabled false --comment "emergency disable — P1 latency spike"
redwoodctl route set --model llama-prod-v3 --variant stable --traffic 100
```

kevin: submitted. API returned 202; change rolling out to edge control plane.
incident-bot: ROUTE CHANGE ACCEPTED — change id rc_4b9f. Propagating to regions us-west1/us-east1.
sophie: seeing traffic drop on canary in apm, stable absorbing traffic. 5xx fraction falling already in us-east1.
alex: applying emergency key throttles for heavy keys that hit >100 req/s to limit spike risk. command:
```
curl -X POST -H "Authorization: Bearer $ADMIN_TOKEN" https://admin.redwood.ai/internal/quotas/emergency \
  -d '{"action":"throttle","match":"api_key:*","rate":50}'
```
maria: any customer impact to callouts/realtime users yet? infra shows some timeouts surfaced to a small subset of premium customers during the peak window.
kevin: we should send a brief note to SRE on-call and Customer Success to prepare comms. @sophie can you capture which keys saw timeouts and approximate window?
sophie: pulling from logs. keys impacted: prod-cust-42, prod-cust-77, prod-cust-99. window approx 15:03–15:12 UTC. counts: 12 timeouts for cust-42, 5 for cust-77, 3 for cust-99.
maria: thanks. I'll start drafting a short customer ping (internal first). Also moving pager to handoff to @kevin in 30m unless cleared.
kevin: oncall-rotation noted. I'm staying primary for mitigation until cleared.
alex: we should leave the canary variant disabled for now and make a ticket to debug model-v3 change set (tokenizer tweak?) before re-enabling. do not re-enable from console without an RCA.
maria: agree. created INC-2026-045-TRACE in bugtracker and linked logs. setting follow-up tasks: reproducer, model artifact diff, kernel perf traces, region breakdown.
incident-bot: INCIDENT UPDATE: status -> mitigation in progress. mitigations: variant disabled, traffic rerouted, emergency throttles applied. Assigned: maria, kevin.
kevin: monitoring for 10m to ensure stable p95 stays under 250ms and 5xx < 1% before we close paging.
sophie: metrics look stable now: p95 ~ 180ms, 5xx ~ 0.6% across regions.
maria: preparing handoff: will update rotation in 25m. please note we still need to run a graded rollout test after root cause is fixed.
alex: ops note for runbook: when disabling a variant, use `variants update --enabled false` and immediately set route traffic to an available stable variant. do not remove variant metadata; keep for forensics.
kevin: added a temporary dashboard widget to show canary traffic 0 and stable traffic 100. saving snapshots.
maria: OK closing pager for now. incident-bot, please set status -> monitoring and add incident tag: "variant-disabled-fallback".
incident-bot: INCIDENT RESOLVED (mitigation): status -> monitoring. NEXT: postmortem assigned to eng-ml (sophie, kevin). ETA 72h.
alex: postmortem should include perf regression test & model artifact diff. assign to research also.
maria: thanks team. I'll follow up with Customer Success for a brief FYI to affected customers. reopening if anything spikes.
kevin: leaving final note: do not re-enable canary until kernel & tokenizer perf tested on full load. added that to the ticket.

(reacts: :white_check_mark: alex, :eyes: sophie)
